issues.description: The template's Farm.singFarmSongVerse method is declared without a parameter (singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)), while the problem UML and the solution expect singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This mismatch can confuse students about the intended method signature and will force them to change the method declaration when implementing the song logic and calling it from singFarmSong().
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to accept an Animal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) and update the method body to use that parameter. This aligns the template with the UML and the solution and avoids unnecessary confusion.

issues.description: The commented example code in the template Main calls farm.feed(), but the problem statement and solution define the corresponding method as feedAllAnimals(). The discrepancy in method name/signature in the template example may mislead students about which API to implement and use.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the commented example in the template Main to call the correct method name (feedAllAnimals()) to match the specification and solution, or add a delegating farm.feed() method in the template that calls feedAllAnimals(), so students are not confused about the expected API.

issues.description: The template's Main.java calls farm.feed(), but the problem statement and the solution use the method name feedAllAnimals(). This mismatch between 'feed' and 'feedAllAnimals' can confuse students when they try to map the requirement (feedAllAnimals) to the starter code (which references feed()).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming consistent: edit src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java in the template to call farm.feedAllAnimals() instead of farm.feed(); or alternatively add a feed() method in Farm that delegates to feedAllAnimals(). Prefer aligning the template with the problem statement by using feedAllAnimals() throughout.
